notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (product analytics) evaluating Redwood for search and chat augmentation. Started on Hosted API (POC ran feb) — good quality, saw 30% latency improvement over current self-hosted embedder. Now in procurement for Dedicated reserved capacity. Negotiation points: commit sizing, burst capacity, overage rates, and a practical ramp schedule to align with Copperfrost's Q2 budget.

POC highlights / Tech: 
- Workloads: chat support (low-latency chat threads), semantic search embeddings (2M vectors/mo), reranking for search results.
- Targets: chat p95 <150ms, throughput baseline 40 req/s with spikes to 120 req/s during peak; embeddings latency <50ms for batch upsert.
- Model preference: open 13B-like weights; want quantized 4-bit for cost efficiency. Agreed to Redwood "verified" model variants for parity testing.

Commercials discussed (notes from 3/05 & 3/10 calls):
- Baseline proposal (A): Dedicated Starter - reserved pool equivalent to 1x 80k tokens/day average; $6k/month committed. Burst allowed 2x baseline 3 hours/day at no extra charge; overage billed at $0.0008/token. (Rough example numbers only)
- Baseline proposal (B): Dedicated Growth - reserved pool 3x 80k tokens/day (~240k/day); $16k/month committed. Burst to 4x baseline for short windows; overage $0.0005/token.
- Copperfrost counter: wants a 6-month ramp: start at Growth/50% capacity first 2 months, full commit by month 4. Requests a graduated discount on overages after ramp complete.
- Redwood options: offer a ramp schedule with step-down overage rates and a 10% credit for missed latency SLA in first 60 days.
- Burst & autoscale: engineering needs clarity on maximum sustained burst and preemption policy. SE Priya to follow up with throughput model and example billing scenarios.

Legal / Security: 
- Copperfrost requires SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logging, KMS integration, and EU data residency for some customer segments. Security FAQ provided: linked.
- DPA reviewed by Copperfrost legal; they requested clarifications on retention windows and subprocessors. Blocker until DPA redlines are reconciled.

Quotes / ARR expectation:
- Copperfrost internal ask: keep ARR under $200k for first year; looking for predictable monthly commit, not usage-only. Their finance team prefers monthly invoicing or quarterly billed commits.
- AE Alex proposed a mid-market pack (Growth) as best fit; final pricing contingent on ramp commitment and term length (12 vs 24 months).

Next steps / Action items:
- Alex to send revised term sheet w/ explicit ramp schedule and example billing (by 2026-03-15).
- Priya to produce throughput-to-cost scenarios and a technical appendix describing KV caching and prefix hot-path for chat (by 2026-03-18).
- Legal: exchange DPA redlines; schedule legal touchpoint (Copperfrost legal + Redwood counsel) 2026-03-22.
- Commercial: schedule final pricing review with VP of Finance at Copperfrost (requested week of 2026-03-29).

Quotes from buyer: "We need predictable monthly economics — burst is fine, but overages scare our CFO. If you give us a clear ramp and capped overage tiers we'll sign 12 months."  - Head of Product, Copperfrost

Misc: internal note - consider offering a performance incentive (first-month credit) to accelerate close. Jira ticket INF-11234 opened for requested throughput report.
